note: La as the step above Sol: a Sol La Sol tune learned in named stages (with the tune, Tune muted, Chords muted), then the home chord's notes over a backing track of the 1st and 5th chords, written as chord tokens and counted the long way, ending in a line of the singer's own. The old Key selector is now moves (any key, 40 to 60 bpm), and the backing track starts at a beginner's 40 with the tune; the made-up line carries the care line.

exercise.title: Sol La Sol, then over chords
exercise.why: La is the step above Sol that tunes lean on and fall back from, so a tune on the two is the first move away from the home chord.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. Sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once La sits one clean step above Sol, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, but La is still one step above Sol.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together. The backing track plays {{chord:I}} and {{chord:V}} in turn, one bar each.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:V}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}. Sing the low {{1}} or {{3}} over {{chord:I}}, and {{5}} over {{chord:V}}. Sing it on "oo".
Then make up your own line from the three notes, one that moves when the chord does.
_Don't reach for high notes: start from the low {{1}} and stay near it._
